file_dispositions.source_contract: FD close returns bool; POSIX unmap is void and ignores msync/munmap results; sync is a separate result path.

objections.resolution: GBA unload drops the realVf pointer without consuming close's bool; fixture-injected failure before real close does not establish OS close-on-error or retry behavior.
The POSIX unmap implementation ignores both syscall results and cannot report them through the VFile void slot.

unresolved: Real host close failure state and retry safety
Crash, reboot, power-loss, filesystem, and non-POSIX persistence semantics

file_dispositions.source_contract: Borrowed-memory wrappers do not own caller storage; VFileMemChunk owns its anonymous allocation. Memory unmap is a no-op, sync reports success without I/O, and mutable borrowed storage can short-write.

objections.resolution: The constructors, close callbacks, no-op unmap, and in-memory sync semantics distinguish borrowed buffers from owned chunks; this is not durable persistence.
The earlier tranche identifies unchecked anonymous allocation and size_t-to-uint32_t capacity rounding; allocation-failure and boundary behavior remain untested.

unresolved: anonymousMemoryMap/mappedMemoryFree implementation and failure behavior
Allocation failure, large-size overflow, zero-size and short-write caller recovery

file_dispositions.source_contract: stdio close reports fclose failure; sync checks fwrite and fflush; map/unmap and truncate contain void/result-loss paths.

objections.resolution: The source distinguishes fflush/fclose bool results from void unmap/truncate paths; local fixture cases are not proof for every filesystem or caller.
No retry-safe fclose contract or complete fseek/map/truncate short-write matrix is established.

unresolved: Truncate short writes and all seek/map failures
Frontend handling and resource ownership after a failed fclose

file_dispositions.source_contract: VFileOpen dispatches through compile-time backend selection; scalar helpers return the backend's reported count rather than requiring full transfers.

objections.resolution: The source establishes backend-selection branches and count propagation, but not which branch a downstream build selects.
No complete platform/frontend build matrix exists in the review packet.

unresolved: Actual downstream backend configuration

file_dispositions.source_contract: Deinit/mask/load/clone/clean/RTC paths consume VFile methods with distinct signed counts, bools, and void results; several output/teardown outcomes are not propagated uniformly.

objections.resolution: Raw-load write count overwrites the read count and success checks non-negativity; mapped load differs; clone does not check the output write result; mask/unmask and deinit ignore selected results.
RTC read converts signed I/O to size_t before validation; RTC/serialization round trip, cold restart, and durable persistence are not established.

unresolved: Negative/short RTC reads and all savedata I/O failure branches
Complete serializer and frontend consumers
Cold restart and durable persistence

dependency_edges.contract: Abstract signed read/write counts, bool close/sync, void unmap/truncate; concrete backends do not share identical error or ownership semantics.
Compile-time dispatch chooses a backend; savedata and script state wrappers consume VFiles, so test-backend evidence cannot establish all platform paths.
GBA unload, core savedata clone/restore, state declarations, and dirty transition provide distinct callers and result sinks.
Frame-end savedataUpdated notification is a modification event, not a VFile sync, serialization, or persistence result.
Script APIs expose serializer/load booleans and callback names; ignored VFile close/map outcomes and external script consumer behavior remain separate.
Memory VFile growth depends on anonymous mapping and capacity arithmetic; declaration-only identity does not prove allocation bounds or failure recovery.
